seo.description: Essaouira travel guide: UNESCO medina, Skala ramparts, fishing port, Atlantic beach, Mellah, and Gnaoua spirit. Best time to visit, top things to do, and day trips.

name: Essaouira
hero_subtitle: Atlantic trade winds, a UNESCO medina of white and blue, Skala cannons facing the ocean and a working fishing port — Morocco’s windiest, most photogenic coastal town.

info.airport_val: ESU Essaouira · CMN Casablanca · RAK Marrakech

overview.title: Welcome to Essaouira — wind, ramparts and Atlantic light
overview.p1: Essaouira sits on Morocco’s Atlantic coast, about two and a half hours west of Marrakech. Its medina is a UNESCO World Heritage site: straight streets, whitewashed walls, blue shutters and the Skala ramparts lined with old cannons facing the swell.
overview.p2: The fishing port, long beach, artisan souks and the offshore Purple Islands give the town a compact rhythm — walkable walls, seafood by the harbour, and steady trade winds that shaped its reputation with surfers and artists alike.

places.title: Must-visit places in Essaouira
places.subtitle: Medina ramparts, port life and Atlantic sand.

medina.title: Medina & Ramparts
medina.desc: White-and-blue UNESCO medina with straight lanes and sea walls.

skala_ville.title: Skala de la Ville
skala_ville.desc: Cannon platform above the ocean — classic Essaouira viewpoint.

skala_port.title: Skala du Port
skala_port.desc: Fortified port ramparts with views over boats and the islands.

port.title: Fishing Port
port.desc: Blue boats, morning catch and grilled fish stalls by the water.

plage.title: Essaouira Beach
plage.desc: Wide Atlantic sand for walks, kite and sunset — strong winds common.

mellah.title: Mellah
mellah.desc: Historic Jewish quarter lanes within the medina fabric.

iles.title: Îles Purpuraires
iles.desc: Rocky islands offshore — views from the Skala; boat trips when seas allow.

souks.title: Souks & Artisan Quarter
souks.desc: Thuya wood, silver jewellery and spice alleys in the medina.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-day plan for Essaouira
itinerary.subtitle: Ramparts and port first, then beach and islands light, with a slower craft day.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Enter the UNESCO white-and-blue medina; walk the Skala de la Ville walls above the Atlantic.
detailed_itinerary.day1_a: Afternoon — Port and Skala du Port
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Fishing harbour, blue boats and the port scale for cannons and sea views.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Quiet lanes of the old Jewish quarter, then seafood near the port or a medina riad courtyard.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Long Atlantic sand south of the walls — walk, kite watch or light swim if conditions allow.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Woodwork, thuya, silver and spice streets inside the medina.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Back to the Skala for wind and golden light over the islands.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Boat to the Îles Purpuraires when allowed, or a slower medina morning.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: More sand time, or a short hop toward Diabat and the coastal dunes.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Last port walk, or road links toward Marrakech or Agadir depending on your route.

bargain.title: Wind & sun

q1.question: How many days in Essaouira?
q1.answer: Two full days cover the medina, Skala, port and beach. Three days allow a slower pace or a coastal day trip.

q2.question: Is Essaouira very windy?
q2.answer: Yes — the alizé is part of its identity. Great for atmosphere and kite sports; bring a layer for the ramparts.

q3.question: How do I get to Essaouira?
q3.answer: ESU airport has seasonal flights. Buses and private transfers link Marrakech (≈2.5 h) and Casablanca. Roads are straightforward.

q4.question: Best time to visit?
q4.answer: Spring and early autumn for milder wind and pleasant temperatures. Summer is lively but breezy; winter is quieter and cooler.
